extracted.intended_audience: international depositary authorities, depositors (biotech patent applicants), industrial property/patent offices and intergovernmental industrial property organizations
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules governing deposit, storage, testing, receipt, transfer and furnishing of microorganisms under the Budapest Treaty for patent procedures, specifying obligations of international depositary authorities, required depositor statements, timelines, communications and conditions for furnishing samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: 'Treaty', 'Article', 'Signature' (Rule 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Treaty" means the Budapest Treaty on the International Recognition of the Deposit of Microorganisms for the Purposes of Patent Procedure; "Article" refers to the specified Article of the Treaty; "signature" shall be understood to mean "seal" where national law requires a seal instead of a signature for an international depositary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation guidance for terminology throughout the Regulations; ensures uniform meaning across rules and accommodates national legal practice regarding seals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal status of International Depositary Authorities (Rule 2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any international depositary authority may be a government agency, including public institutions attached to public administration other than the central government, or a private entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets allowable legal organizational forms for institutions that may acquire IDA status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff and facilities requirements for IDAs (Rule 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The staff and facilities must enable storage of deposited microorganisms so they are kept viable and uncontaminated and must provide sufficient safety measures to minimize risk of loss of microorganisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies practical performance standards: capability to store, maintain viability, prevent contamination and safety measures to avoid loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples obligation for IDAs (Rule 2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any international depositary authority must furnish samples of deposited microorganisms in an expeditious and proper manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes expectation of prompt and appropriate response when furnishing requested samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication to acquire IDA status: addressing and required contents (Rule 3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication (Article 7(1)) must be addressed to Director General via diplomatic channels for Contracting States or by chief executive officer for intergovernmental organizations, and must indicate: (i) name and address of the depositary institution; (ii) detailed information on capacity to comply with Article 6(2) (legal status, scientific standing, staff and facilities); (iii) specify kinds of microorganisms accepted if limited; (iv) indicate fees for storage, viability statements and furnishing samples; (v) indicate official language(s) of the institution; (vi) where applicable, indicate the date referred to in Article 7(1)(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the informational and procedural content required for an entity to notify intent to become an IDA; includes administrative and operational details and language designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of communication and publication (Rule 3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the communication complies with Article 7(1) and Rule 3.1, the Director General shall promptly notify all Contracting States and intergovernmental industrial property organizations and the International Bureau shall promptly publish it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation of the International Bureau/Director General to promptly notify and publish compliant acquisition communications to ensure transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of kinds of microorganisms accepted (Rule 3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Contracting State or organization may later notify extension of assurances to additional specified kinds of microorganisms; Article 7 and Rules 3.1 and 3.2 apply mutatis mutandis for those additional kinds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows IDAs to expand scope post-notification; such extensions follow the same procedural rules as initial communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request and processing for termination/limitation of IDA status (Rule 4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request (Article 8(1)(a)) must be addressed to Director General as in Rule 3.1(a) and shall: (i) indicate name and address of the IDA; (ii) specify kinds if limited; (iii) indicate in detail the facts on which it is based. If compliant, Director General notifies Contracting States and organizations. Assembly shall consider request not earlier than six and not later than eight months from notification unless Director General convenes earlier to protect depositors. If Assembly decides to terminate or limit status, decision becomes effective three months after the date it was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets procedural timeline and content for termination/limitation requests and provides protective measure allowing earlier consideration where depositors' interests are endangered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication, effective date and processing for termination (Rule 4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications under Article 8(2)(a) must be addressed to Director General, indicate name/address of IDA, specify kinds if limited, and may indicate a later effective date if desired. Effects occur on the indicated later date or, if none indicated, three months from communication. Director General shall promptly notify Contracting States and organizations and International Bureau shall publish notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mechanism to delay effective date of communicated termination and mandates prompt notification/publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for deposits upon termination/limitation (Rule 4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of termination/limitation of IDA status under Articles 8(1), 8(2), 9(4) or 17(4), Rule 5.1 shall apply mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References obligations for transfer and protection of deposits in the event of termination/limitation (see Rule 5.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations on discontinuance of IDA functions (Rule 5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IDA temporarily or definitively discontinues performance of tasks under the Treaty for deposited microorganisms, the Contracting State or organization which furnished assurances shall: (i) ensure, to fullest extent possible, prompt transfer of samples without deterioration/contamination to a substitute authority; (ii) ensure transfer of mail, communications, files and other relevant information to substitute authority; (iii) ensure prompt notification to affected depositors of discontinuance and transfers; (iv) promptly notify Director General of facts and measures taken. Director General shall notify Contracting States and offices and publish notifications. Depositors may be required to notify industrial property offices of new accession numbers; substitute authority shall retain previous accession number together with new one. Depositor may request transfer of samples to another authority (at depositor's expense) and defaulting authority shall retain samples on request as far as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive protective duties to preserve depositor rights and biological material integrity in case of IDA default; includes administrative continuity and information-transfer obligations and depositor options for further transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal by IDA to accept kinds it should accept (Rule 5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IDA refuses to accept for deposit any kinds of microorganisms which it should accept under its assurances, the Contracting State or organization shall promptly notify Director General of facts and measures taken; Director General shall notify others and publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates transparency and oversight when an IDA deviates from its declared scope of accepted microorganisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original deposit: required written statement contents (Rule 6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Microorganism transmitted to IDA (except where Rule 6.2 applies) must be accompanied by a written statement bearing depositor's signature containing: (i) indication deposit is made under the Treaty and undertaking not to withdraw it for period in Rule 9.1; (ii) name and address of depositor; (iii) details of conditions necessary for cultivation, storage and viability testing and, if a mixture, descriptions of components and at least one method permitting checking of their presence; (iv) identification reference given by depositor; (v) indication of properties dangerous to health/environment or indication depositor not aware of such properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies essential technical, safety and administrative data the depositor must supply to enable storage, testing and safe handling and to link deposit to patent procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: include scientific description/taxonomic designation (Rule 6.1(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: It is strongly recommended that the written statement contain the scientific description and/or proposed taxonomic designation of the deposited microorganism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not mandatory but recommended for clarity and identification purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: New deposit: required documents and statement contents (Rule 6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a new deposit under Article 4, the microorganism must be accompanied by copy of receipt of previous deposit, copy of most recent viability statement indicating microorganism is viable, and a written statement bearing depositor's signature containing: (i) the indications in Rule 6.1(a)(i)-(v); (ii) declaration stating reason relevant under Article 4(1)(a) for making new deposit, statement alleging the microorganism is same as previous deposit, and indication of date depositor received notification under Article 4(1)(a) or publication date under Article 4(1)(e); (iii) where prior scientific description/designation was indicated, the most recent such description/designation as communicated with previous deposit. "Previous deposit" defined in Rule 6.2(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines evidentiary and descriptive requirements to link a new deposit to a prior deposit and to document reasons/timing for new deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDA may impose administrative requirements (Rule 6.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA may require: (i) deposit in form/quantity necessary for Treaty purposes; (ii) completion of forms established by authority for administrative procedures; (iii) that the written statement be drafted in language(s) specified by the authority (must include the official language(s) indicated under Rule 3.1(b)(v)); (iv) payment of storage fee under Rule 12.1(a)(i); (v) that, to extent permitted by law, depositor enter into a contract defining liabilities of depositor and authority. Any such requirements and amendments must be communicated to the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows IDAs to set reasonable administrative, linguistic, financial and contractual prerequisites but requires notification of such requirements to International Bureau for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance procedure: grounds for refusal and acceptance (Rule 6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: IDA shall refuse to accept microorganism and immediately notify depositor in writing with reasons if: (i) microorganism is not of a kind to which assurances extend; (ii) properties are so exceptional IDA is technically unable to perform required tasks; (iii) deposit is received in condition indicating microorganism missing or acceptance precluded for scientific reasons. Subject to above, IDA shall accept when all requirements of Rule 6.1(a) or 6.2(a) and Rule 6.3(a) are complied with; if not complied with IDA shall notify depositor and invite compliance. Date of original/new deposit is date received by IDA. IDA may, on request and if requirements complied with, consider a deposit made before it acquired IDA status to have been received on date its status was acquired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines objective technical and administrative grounds for refusal, acceptance conditions, and rules for establishing deposit date (including treatment of pre-status deposits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of receipt for each deposit (Rule 7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IDA shall issue to the depositor, for each deposit effected with it or transferred to it, a receipt attesting it has received and accepted the microorganism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal proof of deposit/acceptance required for patent procedure linkage and administrative records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, languages and signature of receipts (Rule 7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipts shall be on an "international form" model established by Director General in languages designated by the Assembly; any words/letters filled in characters other than Latin alphabet shall be transliterated into Latin characters; receipt shall bear signature of person(s) with power to represent the IDA or of an authorized official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardizes receipt format, language transcription and authorized signature to ensure international readability and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in receipt for original deposit (Rule 7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt for original deposit shall indicate IDA issued it under the Treaty and contain at least: (i) name and address of IDA; (ii) name and address of depositor; (iii) date of original deposit as defined in Rule 6.4(c); (iv) identification reference given by depositor; (v) accession number given by IDA; (vi) where written statement contained scientific description and/or proposed taxonomic designation, a reference to that fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies minimum data elements the receipt must include to identify and link deposit to depositor and patent filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in receipt for new deposit (Rule 7.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt for new deposit under Article 4 shall be accompanied by copy of previous receipt and most recent viability statement indicating viability, and shall contain at least: (i) name and address of IDA; (ii) name and address of depositor; (iii) date of new deposit as defined in Rule 6.4(c); (iv) identification reference given by depositor; (v) accession number given to new deposit; (vi) indication of relevant reason and date as stated by depositor under Rule 6.2(a)(ii); (vii) where Rule 6.2(a)(iii) applies, reference to fact scientific description/designation indicated; (viii) accession number given to previous deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures continuity and traceability between new and previous deposits, and documents reasons and dates related to Article 4 events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt contents in case of transfer (Rule 7.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IDA to which samples are transferred under Rule 5.1(a)(i) shall issue to depositor a receipt indicating IDA capacity under Treaty and containing at least: (i) name and address of IDA; (ii) name and address of depositor; (iii) date transferred sample was received by IDA (date of transfer); (iv) identification reference given by depositor; (v) accession number given by IDA; (vi) name and address of IDA from which transfer was effected; (vii) accession number given by IDA from which transfer was effected; (viii) where written statement contained scientific description/designation or it was indicated/amended under Rule 8.1, reference to that fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents transfer events and cross-references accession numbers to preserve chain-of-custody and traceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of scientific description/taxonomic designation on request (Rule 7.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: On request of any party entitled to receive a sample under Rules 11.1, 11.2 or 11.3, IDA shall communicate to such party the most recent scientific description and/or proposed taxonomic designation referred to in Rules 6.1(b), 6.2(a)(iii) or 8.1(b)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation to provide up-to-date descriptive information accompanying furnished samples to entitled parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Later indication or amendment of scientific description/taxonomic designation (Rule 8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositor may later indicate or amend scientific description and/or taxonomic designation in a written communication bearing depositor's signature addressed to the IDA, containing: (i) depositor name and address; (ii) accession number; (iii) scientific description and/or proposed taxonomic designation; (iv) in case of amendment, the last preceding scientific description and/or proposed taxonomic designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mechanism for updating identification data post-deposit; requires signature and accession linkage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation upon later indication/amendment (Rule 8.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: On request of depositor who made the communication under Rule 8.1, IDA shall deliver an attestation showing the data referred to in Rule 8.1(b)(i)-(iv) and the date of receipt of such communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDA must provide written proof of receipt and contents of subsequent description/amendment communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of storage obligations (Rule 9.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any microorganism deposited shall be stored by the IDA with all care necessary to keep it viable and uncontaminated for at least five years after the most recent request for furnishing of a sample was received and, in any case, for at least 30 years after date of deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum retention periods ensuring availability for patent procedures and requests; coupled with care obligations to maintain viability and prevent contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy and confidentiality of deposits (Rule 9.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: No IDA shall give information to anyone whether a microorganism has been deposited with it under the Treaty, nor give any information concerning any deposited microorganism except to an authority, person or legal entity entitled to obtain a sample under Rule 11 and subject to the same conditions as in that Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong confidentiality protection over the existence and details of deposits, with disclosure limited strictly to entitled parties and under Rule 11 conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to test viability: timing and conditions (Rule 10.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: IDA shall test viability of each deposited microorganism: (i) promptly after any deposit referred to in Rule 6 or any transfer referred to in Rule 5.1; (ii) at reasonable intervals depending on kind of microorganism and storage conditions, or at any time if necessary for technical reasons; (iii) at any time on request of depositor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines mandatory testing schedule and discretionary/need-based testing to ensure viability is monitored appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability statement: recipients, contents, form and fees (Rule 10.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: IDA shall issue a viability statement: (a)(i) to depositor promptly after any deposit or transfer; (ii) to depositor on request at any time after deposit/transfer; (iii) to any industrial property office, other authority, person or legal entity (other than depositor) to whom samples were furnished under Rule 11, on request together with or at any time after such furnishing. Statement shall indicate whether microorganism is or is no longer viable and contain: (i) name and address of IDA issuing it; (ii) name and address of depositor; (iii) the deposit date(s) as applicable; (iv) accession number; (v) date of the test to which it refers; (vi) information on conditions under which test performed, provided such information requested and results were negative. Statement shall refer to most recent viability test where applicable; form/languages/signature per Rule 7.2 apply mutatis mutandis. Issuance shall be free of charge in cases of (a)(i) and where request is made by an industrial property office; other viability statements may be charged (Rule 12.1(a)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies who may obtain viability evidence, the required content for legal/technical use, cost exemptions and format consistency with receipts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing samples to interested industrial property offices: conditions (Rule 11.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: IDA shall furnish a sample to any industrial property office of any Contracting State or intergovernmental industrial property organization on request provided request is accompanied by a declaration that: (i) an application referring to the deposit has been filed with that office for grant of a patent and subject matter involves the microorganism or its use; (ii) such application is pending or has led to grant of patent; (iii) sample is needed for purposes of a patent procedure having effect in that Contracting State/organization; (iv) sample and any information accompanying or resulting from it will be used only for purposes of the said patent procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits furnishing to patent-related, legitimate procedural needs and requires declaration of intended use and application status to protect confidentiality and lawful use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing to depositor or authorized party (Rule 11.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: IDA shall furnish a sample: (i) to depositor on request; (ii) to any authority, natural person or legal entity ("authorized party") on request provided request is accompanied by depositor's declaration authorizing the requested furnishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures depositor control over third-party access by requiring explicit authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing to parties legally entitled (certified party) and certification form (Rule 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: IDA shall furnish a sample to a certified party on request where request is made on a form whose contents are fixed by the Assembly and the industrial property office certifies: (i) that an application referring to the deposit has been filed and subject matter involves the microorganism; (ii) that publication for patent procedure purposes has been effected by that office (except where second phrase of (iii) applies); (iii) either that certified party has a right to a sample under the law governing patent procedure before that office and, where right depends on fulfillment of conditions, that office is satisfied conditions have been fulfilled, or that certified party has affixed signature on a form before that office rendering conditions deemed fulfilled; where certified party's right exists before publication and publication not yet effected, certification must state so and cite applicable provision of law including court decisions. Additionally, industrial property offices may communicate lists of accession numbers of deposited microorganisms referred to in patents and IDA shall furnish sample on request where accession number has been communicated (in which case certification of Rule 11.3(a) not required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets detailed legal-certification procedure linking national patent-law entitlement to access; also provides alternative route via accession-number lists for published patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common rules for requests/declarations/certifications (Rule 11.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests/declarations/certifications/communications under Rules 11.1-11.3 must: (a)(i) be in English, French, Russian or Spanish when addressed to an IDA whose official language includes one of those (with certified translation provisions); (ii) otherwise in English or French or in official language of the IDA; (b) special translation provisions when request comes from office whose official language is Russian or Spanish; (c) be in writing, bear a signature and be dated; (d) contain indications: (i) name and address of the industrial property office/authorized/certified party; (ii) accession number given to deposit; (iii) for Rule 11.1, date and number of application or patent referring to deposit; (iv) for Rule 11.3(a), indications referred to in (iii) and name and address of office making certification; (e) requests under Rule 11.3(b) shall contain name and address of requesting party and accession number; (f) container for furnished sample shall be marked with accession number and accompanied by copy of receipt referred to in Rule 7, indication of any properties dangerous to health or environment and, upon request, indication of conditions employed for cultivation and storage; (g) ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardizes procedural, linguistic, documentary and safety information requirements for all sample furnishing operations; mandates translations, signatures, dates and content elements to ensure legal validity and safe handling. (Note: Rule 11.4(g) continues beyond provided excerpt.)
